title: Programming in C
blurb: Start from zero and learn to think like a programmer in C: variables, decisions, loops, functions, arrays, strings, pointers, memory, structures and files.
learn: Write, compile and run complete C programs
Use `if`, `switch` and loops to solve pattern and number problems
Break programs into functions and solve problems recursively
Work with arrays, strings and 2D matrices
Understand pointers, addresses and dynamic memory
Model data with structures and save it to files

title: Data Structures
blurb: Build every classic data structure in C — linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, heaps, graphs and hash tables — and learn exactly when to use each one.
learn: Measure code with Big-O time and space complexity
Implement linked lists, stacks and queues from scratch
Build and traverse binary trees, BSTs, AVL trees and heaps
Represent graphs and run BFS and DFS
Use hashing and resolve collisions
Pick the right searching and sorting algorithm

title: Object-Oriented Programming with C++
blurb: Move from C to C++ and master object-oriented design: classes, constructors, inheritance, polymorphism, templates, exceptions and the STL.
learn: Explain the four pillars of OOP with real code
Design classes with constructors, destructors and access control
Use inheritance, virtual functions and abstract classes
Overload functions and operators
Write generic code with templates
Use STL containers and algorithms productively

title: Python Programming
blurb: Python from first print() to real programs: data types, control flow, lists, dictionaries, functions, files, exceptions, OOP and generators.
learn: Write clean Python with the right built-in types
Use lists, tuples, sets and dictionaries fluently
Write reusable functions, lambdas and comprehensions
Read and write files and handle errors gracefully
Build classes with inheritance and dunder methods
Use iterators, generators and the standard library

title: Discrete Mathematics
blurb: The mathematics under computer science: logic, proofs, sets, relations, functions, counting, recurrences, graph theory, number theory and Boolean algebra.
learn: Build truth tables and simplify logical expressions
Write direct, contradiction and induction proofs
Work with sets, relations, functions and partial orders
Count with permutations, combinations and inclusion–exclusion
Solve recurrence relations
Reason about graphs, trees, modular arithmetic and Boolean algebra

title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
blurb: Analyse and design efficient algorithms: asymptotic analysis, recurrences, divide and conquer, greedy methods, dynamic programming, backtracking, graph algorithms and NP-completeness.
learn: Analyse running time with O, Ω and Θ
Solve recurrences with the Master Theorem
Design divide-and-conquer and greedy algorithms
Solve problems with dynamic programming tables
Use backtracking and branch and bound
Explain P, NP, NP-complete and NP-hard

title: First-Year Foundations
blurb: How computers, code and the web really work: number systems, logic gates, algorithms and flowcharts, the Linux terminal, Git and GitHub, HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
learn: Explain what happens inside a computer when a program runs
Convert between binary, octal, decimal and hexadecimal
Plan solutions with algorithms, flowcharts and pseudocode
Get comfortable in the Linux command line
Use Git and GitHub to save and share your work
Build a simple web page with HTML, CSS and JavaScript
